answer: Operator-Linked Identity Ledger. Each agent identity is bound to an operator's persistent ledger entry, and every new identity under that operator multiplies a per-identity surcharge derived from a rotating cipher of the prior registration batch. A sybil cluster collapses to one operator line, so N identities cost roughly N² in good standing. The operator's ledger is placed on a shared verification vertex, making the surcharge visible to all counterparties. Deception also freezes the operator's mesa of pending settlements until reconciled.
